The '''International Mathematical Modeling Challenge (IMMC''' or sometimes '''IM<sup>2</sup>C)''' is an international [[mathematical modeling competition]] for high school students in team [[mathematical model]]ing co-sponsored by COMAP<ref name="COMAP">{{Cite web|url=https://www.comap.com/|title=Mathematics Resources and Contests - Consortium for Mathematics and its Applications - COMAP|website=www.comap.com}}</ref> and the NeoUnion ESC Organization.<ref name="NeoUnion">{{Cite web|url=https://www.neounion.net/|title=Home|website=NeoUnion}}</ref><ref name="ICIAM">[http://www.iciam2015.cn/MS-Fr-D-67.html International Conference on Industrial and Applied Mathematics]</ref> Teams are selected on a country-by-country basis, with each country sending up to two teams to the competition. The IMMC was inspired by the High School Mathematical Contest in Modeling (HiMCM), a similar contest sponsored by COMAP but mainly attracting teams within the United States.<ref name="HiMCM">{{Cite web|url=https://www.contest.comap.com/highschool/contests/himcm/index.html|title=COMAP: Mathematics Instructional Resources for Innovative Educators|website=www.contest.comap.com}}</ref> The HiMCM in turn was established in the 1990s to create a high school counterpart to COMAP’s [[Mathematical Contest in Modeling|MCM]].<ref name="IMMC Origins">[https://www.facebook.com/immchallenge/photos/pb.1746968815530398.-2207520000.1444424370./1747227858837827/?type=3&theater IMMC PowerPoint Posted on IMM Challenge Official Facebook Page]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/rbr/files/bmtc-5-30-slides.pdf|title = Harvard University -- A Placement Problem|date = |accessdate = |website = |publisher = |last = |first = }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.mathmodels.org/contests.html|title = Mathematical Modeling Contests|date = |accessdate = |website = |publisher = |last = |first = }}</ref> Contestants in the IMMC are given five days to research (the contest permits the use of any inanimate source) and write a mathematical paper detailing their mathematical model for a given situation.<ref name="IMMC Rules">{{Cite web|url=https://www.immchallenge.org/Pages/Rules.html|title=The International Mathematical Modeling Challenge (IMMC)|website=www.immchallenge.org}}</ref> At the conclusion of the five-day period, papers are sent to an international expert committee composed of mathematics faculty from the world’s leading universities. Traditionally, 2-4 teams are awarded the top designation of Outstanding and invited to an awards ceremony, held in a different country or region each year.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.utdanacenter.org/wp-content/uploads/teaching_matters_umln_2-10-15.pdf|title = National Council of Teachers of Mathematics -- Teaching Matters!|date = |accessdate = |website = |publisher = |last = |first = |archive-date = 2016-08-14|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160814033010/http://www.utdanacenter.org/wp-content/uploads/teaching_matters_umln_2-10-15.pdf|url-status = dead}}</ref>

==Team selection==
Each participating country is expected to choose its two best teams of one to four contestants each to compete in the IMMC. Globally, different methods have been used to select teams from their respective countries.

Hong Kong holds the contest early and allows any interested team to participate.<ref name="CUMCM">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mcm.edu.cn/html_cn/node/4a8cd11cda4e98ed825dffa50e5bc7b3.html|title=全国大学生数学建模竞赛|website=www.mcm.edu.cn}}</ref> A national judging panel selects the two best papers to move on to the international round of the competition. In 2015, 60 papers came out of the Greater China region alone.<ref name="Greater China Teams">{{Cite web|url=https://www.polyu.edu.hk/ama/CAM/cam-digest-html/15/v15n15.html|title=CAM Digest, V. 15, # 15|website=www.polyu.edu.hk}}</ref>

In 2015, the United States used a different qualification process, inviting the top two teams from the 2014 HiMCM to compete in the IMMC. In 2016, the United States adopted a hybrid of Hong Kong’s approach and its own former approach: any team receiving a score of Meritorious or higher in the 2015 HiMCM (roughly 25% of competing teams) was invited to compete in the 2016 IMMC. As in Hong Kong, the United States held the IMMC early, completed a national round of judging, and selected the two best papers to move on to the international round.<ref name="USA Rules">{{Cite web|url=https://immchallenge.org/Pages/Rules/USA/USA-Rules.html|title=The International Mathematical Modeling Challenge (IMMC)|website=immchallenge.org}}</ref>

Most countries use a selection process similar to that used by Hong Kong, and countries entering the IMMC for the first time will also likely adopt a similar process.<ref name="UUIMMC">{{Cite web |url=http://www.fisme.science.uu.nl/wiki/index.php/International_Mathematical_Modeling_Challenge |title=University of Utrecht -- International Mathematical Modeling Challenge |access-date=2015-10-13 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304185635/http://www.fisme.science.uu.nl/wiki/index.php/International_Mathematical_Modeling_Challenge |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.mathschool.ru/page/224.html|title = Математическая школа -- Международный конкурс "Математическое моделирование"|date = |accessdate = |website = |publisher = |last = |first = }}</ref>

==Judging==
Papers passing the national selection round move on to the international expert judging panel.
